title: Team Assistant - Fleet
description:
We have a great opportunity that has arisen within our Direct Services team for a Team Assistant. You'll be providing a full range of administrative and support services, ranging from moderate to complex, to facilitate the effective and efficient operation of the team/department.

Some key duties will include:
- Developing and maintaining administrative and office systems, databases/spreadsheets, online Fleet related platforms such as Licence check, tracking, TFL, Insurance etc as required.
- Booking vehicles in for relevant maintenance (MOT, Service, repairs), updating calendars and communicating back to drivers/managers.
- Arranging, and attending or representing unit/supervisor at meetings, including preparing papers, booking rooms, taking notes, and drafting minutes.
- Intercepting and screening telephone calls, emails and written correspondence, dealing with, or redirecting enquiries to the appropriate areas/managers, as necessary.
- Providing project support to the team and to lead on administrative projects such as fuel audits, insurance audits, key audits etc as required.

This is a 12-Month Secondment / Fixed Term Contract working 24 hours a week. Your main site will be The Tramsheds, Croydon, with a requirement to work on onsite at least 2 days a week.

What you'll have
- Experience in an Administrative role.
- Fleet experience or adjacent is desirable but not essential.
- Computer skills sufficient to operate on-line system and complex software or develop formulas for moderately sophisticated spreadsheets.
- Oral and written communication skills sufficient to interpret and apply policies and procedures and to resolve problems, and to present a professional approach to all customers and stakeholders.
- The ability to use a variety of software packages to produce correspondence and documents, and maintain presentations, spreadsheets and databases.

Advert closing date: 1st November 2026 at 23:59 (We may close the advert early if we receive a suitable number of applications).

About Us

At Southern Housing, our residents are at the heart of everything we do. As one of the largest housing providers in the UK with over 77,000 homes across London, the Southeast, the Isle of Wight, and the Midlands, we give over 167,000 people somewhere affordable to call their own! We also understand the difference that safe, secure, and affordable homes can make to people's lives.

A career at Southern Housing will allow you to make a difference every day you come to work. Working in the housing sector with us will bring fresh challenges and give you the opportunity to grow and develop, too.

title: Finance Officer
description:
About Action Tutoring
At Action Tutoring, we believe every child should be given the opportunity to succeed in school. But in the UK today, young people from disadvantaged backgrounds are less likely to achieve the grades they need to progress in life. This isn't because they are any less able; they have less access to the tools to help them reach their potential.

We don't think this is fair. We know tutoring is an effective way of improving academic attainment and so we harness the power of volunteer tutors to bridge the gap and ensure this help can be accessed by every pupil who needs it, not just those who can afford it.

We specifically help pupils facing socio-economic disadvantage and who are at risk of leaving primary or secondary school without reaching national standards in their exams. We work in partnership with schools in different cities and regions across the UK, delivering weekly tutoring in English or maths to those pupils who need it most.

About the opportunity
The Finance Officer will be responsible for leading the day-to-day finance function and providing support to the Director of Finance & Operations and the wider team on all aspects of the organisation's finances.

This role plays a crucial role in the Operations Team by managing key finance processes, managing key finance systems, supporting budget holders, and ensuring the accuracy of our financial records.

Closing date: Sunday, 22nd November 2026
Interviews: Monday, 30th November 2026
Start date: Ideal start date is asap. However, we're happy to wait for the ideal candidate.
Contract and hours: Permanent. Part-time 0.6 FTE. The successful candidate will be required to work on Mondays and Wednesdays, with the third working day flexible by agreement. A full working week is 37.5 hours.
Place of work: Hybrid / flexible. This role requires 1 day a week in our London Office, Fivefields, Grosvenor Gardens, London SW1 W 0 DH.

Duties and responsibilities
- Ownership of the purchase ledger: maintain full oversight including supplier invoices, obtaining approvals, and managing payments.
- Ownership of the sales ledger: maintain full oversight including raising invoices for schools and funders, generating donation and income receipts, managing aged debtors.
- Ownership of bank reconciliation: manage banking administration and bank reconciliation.
- Ownership of the as the first point of contact and responding to customer and supplier queries.
- Ensure the finance system and financial records are accurate and up to date.
- Any other ad hoc responsibilities as deemed relevant by the CEO.

A full list of duties and responsibilities can be found in the job description attached to the BreatheHR advert.

Person specification

Qualifications Criteria
- Right to work in the UK

We are looking for someone who has:
- Previous experience of working within a finance team managing daily finance transactions and processes
- Experience of working with finance systems
- Excellent attention to detail to ensure accuracy of data
- Strong organisational skills and can manage multiple deadlines
- Very good interpersonal skills and enjoys supporting others
- A proficiency in building relationships both with internal and external stakeholders
- A commitment to personal development
- A commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.
- A commitment to the mission and values of Action Tutoring.
- A commitment to promoting and safeguarding the welfare of children.

You'll likely be more successful in this role if you have:
- An accountancy qualification, part-qualification or studying towards an accountancy qualification
- Experience of using the Twinfield finance system
- Experience of working in a charity

title: Finance & Admin Officer
company: The Linnean Society of London - Agency - Permanent
description:
Key information

Contract: Permanent, part-time, onsite

Salary: £26,936-£33,000 per annum pro rata

Hours/Days of the week: 3 days a week. Ideally Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, 9:30-17:30

Location: The Linnean Society, Burlington Courtyard, Piccadilly, London, W1 J 0 BF

In post: Early 2027 depending on your notice period.

About the role

You will support the Director of Finance in managing the Society's finances and service operations in line with the Society's governing documents, and to ensure compliance with legal and financial responsibilities. You will be responsible for efficiently and accurately recording and processing the Society's day-to-day transactions, performing accounting reconciliations, and administrating the income associated with the Society's services.

Part of your working week will be to work alongside our Operations Assistant at Front of House, providing a welcoming, accessible and safe experience for all our visitors. We anticipate this will comprise approximately 20% of your workload, with the remaining 80% dedicated to finance duties.

About you

You have practical experience working effectively within a finance function, using finance systems and software and proven strong numeracy, accuracy and data analysis skills. Ideally, you are somebody that has had some experience in finance and are now eager to further develop your skills within a finance role.

You bring excellent IT skills, and you readily offer and accept help when needed. Your experience and excellent organisational skills mean you can switch between tasks while maintaining strong attention to detail. Plus, your approachable and adaptable nature allows you to make a positive contribution, even under pressure.

You enjoy engaging with a diverse range of individuals, whether in person, over the telephone, or via email, always doing so with patience, kindness, and calm confidence.

About the Society

We are a not-for-profit organisation and registered charity that delivers our charitable objectives in science, heritage, and education through our activities, events, and publications. Our collections, events and programmes share the vital stories of biodiversity loss and climate change, connecting with people of all ages and backgrounds.

Our mission is to cultivate a global community working for a world where nature is understood, valued, and protected.

About us

We are a not-for-profit organisation and registered charity that delivers our charitable objectives in science, heritage, and education through our activities, events, and publications. Our collections, events and programmes share the vital stories of biodiversity loss and climate change, connecting with people of all ages and backgrounds.

Our mission is to cultivate a global community working for a world where nature is understood, valued, and protected.

We are strongly supported by our growing international membership.

Our offices, library and collection are housed in a Grade II listed building in Burlington Courtyard in Piccadilly, London.

About the team

We are a kind, supportive team of 24 staff, with big ambitions and a huge commitment to the work we do.

We value an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are appreciated, and everyone has the opportunity to contribute, grow, and thrive. We don't look for colleagues who simply fit our current culture; we look for people who expand it. We warmly welcome applications from all eligible candidates, of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences.

Further information

Please note that successful candidate will be asked to evidence their Right to Work in the UK post-job offer - we do not hold a sponsor license therefore we are unable to provide Visa sponsorship.

title: Team Coordinator
description:
Salary: £31,400- £38,300

Closing date:Thursday 5 November 2026

Contract type: permanent

Interview dates: 1st stage; w/c 16 November 2026) online/Remote; 2nd stage: 23 November 2026 face to face

Wellcome Collection is part of Wellcome Trust, a global charitable foundation that supports science to build a healthier future for everyone.

Wellcome Collection is a free museum and library exploring health and human experience, where you can enjoy exhibitions, museum and library collections, public events, and a vibrant shop and café. We also publish books and online stories.

This is a great time to join Wellcome Collection as we embark on an exciting period of development. We are looking for two Team Coordinators to join our business operations team. These roles will play an important part in supporting and enabling our teams to deliver on our vision of a world where everyone's experience of health matters.

Where in Wellcome will I be working?

You will be one of three Team Coordinators working within the Strategy, Delivery & Transformation team, reporting to the Wellcome Collections Operations Manager.

Along with the Operations Manager and your fellow Team Coordinators, you will provide high level administrative support across multiple teams and departments within Wellcome Collection

What will I be doing?

Wellcome Collection is a free museum and library that explores connections between health, life and human experience. We are looking for two highly organised and proactive Team Coordinators to provide essential administrative and operational support to our Directorate and Leadership Team. The roles are central to ensuring the smooth running of day-to-day activities, coordinating key meetings and governance processes, managing office operations, and supporting collaboration across teams. Working closely with colleagues across Wellcome Collection, you will help create an efficient, inclusive and well-connected working environment that enables teams to deliver their objectives and the Wellcome Collection strategy.

In this role, you will:
- Provide high-quality administrative support to the Directorate and Leadership Team, including expenses, invoice processing, purchasing, and managing operational activities.
- Coordinate internal and external meetings, preparing agendas, papers and presentations, taking accurate minutes, and tracking actions to completion.
- Organise all-staff meetings, governance meetings, workshops, training sessions, away days, and provide logistical support for events as required.
- Manage onboarding activities for new team members and arrange occasional travel and accommodation for leaders attending external meetings and conferences.
- Oversee office operations, including supplies, equipment, technology requirements, workspace arrangements, and maintaining accurate databases and records.
- Collaborate with colleagues across Wellcome Collection, contributing to a positive, inclusive culture while ensuring administrative cover and support across teams when needed.

Is this job for me?

To be successful in this role, you will bring previous PA, Executive Assistant or administrative experience gained within a busy and fast-paced environment. You will have excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while working to deadlines. You will be confident building relationships with stakeholders at all levels, handling confidential information with discretion, and communicating clearly in both written and verbal formats. Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including SharePoint, are essential, and experience of would be advantageous.

The ideal candidate will have experience managing calendars, preparing meeting papers and presentations, drafting correspondence, taking minutes, and coordinating complex administrative activities. You will be proactive, resourceful and comfortable taking initiative, with a collaborative approach and a commitment to delivering excellent support. Most importantly, you will thrive in a role where organisation, teamwork and attention to detail are critical to enabling the success of others.

To apply for this role please submit an updated CV and answer 2 application questions to demonstrate that you meet the minimum requirements for the role.

Minimum Criteria:
- Ability to multi-task, prioritise, take initiative and work to deadlines.
- Well-developed time management skills, including ability to prioritise and reprioritise tasks without compromising quality, organising complex itineraries. As well as good verbal and written communication skills.
- Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite of products (eg Word, Outlook, Excel, SharePoint)
- Ability to deal with people at all levels and deal professionally with confidential material and issues.
- A pragmatic, positive attitude with the desire to work within a high performing team

Applications Questions:
- Using examples please provide evidence to demonstrate that you meet the minimum criteria for this role as outlined in the job description? (Up to 500 words)
- Using short summaries please provide specific details of up to two different initiatives or projects you have been directly involved in that are relevant to this role. For each initiative or project please use up to 250 words to describe your role (e.g. team leader, team member), the purpose of the activity (i.e. its aims), and the major contributions you personally made.

You can view the full job description on our website.

You can read more about the benefits we offer our employees on our website

Our Hybrid Way of Working

We understand that our colleagues have commitments and personal interests outside of work and we strive to build a flexible working environment, in which people can perform at their best.

At Wellcome we have a hybrid way of working which is 3 days in our Euston Road offices (Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday) with the remaining 2 days working either remotely or in the office.

With this in mind however, Wellcome Collection is a 7 day per week operation. Therefore, in your role, on occasion it may be necessary for you to attend the office more frequently or support on work or projects outside of usual office hours.

Diversity and Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do

Diversity and Inclusion is a priority at Wellcome . We are committed to cultivating a fair andinclusiveenvironment, where everyone can be themselves and thrive. We are happy to discuss flexible working options for all roles. We work to ensure that our recruitment processes are as inclusive as possible to everyone. This includesmaking adjustmentsfor people who have a disability or long-term condition.Please visit our website for more information on adjustments and accessibility, or contact us at .

title: Receptionist / Admin
description: We are seeking a receptionist to join our practice of 9100+ patients. 37.5 hours per week and must be available for afternoon shifts. Receptionist work is between the hours of 07:45 to 18:30 Monday to Friday. The successful candidate will need to be hard-working, flexible and enthusiastic. We are looking for a capable individual who is able to multi-task and work well under pressure. INTERVIEWS WILL BE HELD VIA TEAMS You must have your covid vaccines to join as a member of the practice. Answering calls Processing prescription Dealing with patient tasks & queries Processing patient administration including snomed coding, typing letters via docman10 Dealing with new patient registrations and deductions Processing recall letters as requested Inputting data into the patient's healthcare records as necessary Supporting clinicians/Practice Manager with general administrative tasks as requested. You will need excellent communication, administrative and IT skills and enjoy working with the general public. Previous experience in a similar position is preferable together with flexibility to cover additional hours are essential. OUTLINE OF DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITES To greet patients in a friendly and courteous manner at all times To answer telephone calls in a polite and professional manner To make appointments for the doctors surgeries and nurses clinics using the Practice clinical information system Answering patient queries regarding various Practice policies and initiatives Advise patient when completing new patient registration forms, explaining the surgery policies To listen to patient complaints, making sure that they are addressed and dealt with appropriately To retrieve patients medical records for various clinics and surgeries and file back patient medical records in the correct order Fax correspondence as requested and record To scan all hospital correspondence accurately using the Docman System Process repeat prescriptions as per the Practice policy Ensure all forms are passed to the appropriate destination and completed and checked by you when required Receiving and recording requests for home visits in line with expected standards Receiving, recording and booking requests for transport Direct accurate patient information to the appropriate clinician using EMIS Web To cover duties for other members of staff, this may arise in the case of absence, sickness and holidays Chaperone GP if required, following training Shared responsibility for reception, waiting rooms and consulting rooms upkeep and tidiness including leaflets and posters To ensure that strict confidentiality protocols are adhered to Attend and contribute to staff meetings To comply with Health & Safety Procedures and report any areas of concern to the Practice Business Manager Opening and closing of premises when required To undertake any other duties as may be determined from time to time to ensure the efficient running of the Practice. Add registrations to the system as per policy Promote, encourage and activate patient on-line access Ensure relevant/appropriate contacts with patients are documented in notes Ensure email, tasks, Docman and EMIS email are checked daily. Open and process post according to agreed practice policy Frank and post out-going mail as per policy Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner that is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, with such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Complete all required regular training Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Ensure you are aware of the organisations safeguarding policys and procedures and know how to action any concerns. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Comply with Information Governance requirements Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist
description: The GP Receptionist is a key front-line role within an NHS GP practice, acting as the first point of contact for patients, carers, and visitors. The role is essential in ensuring the smooth and efficient running of the practice on a daily basis. You will provide a professional, caring, and confidential reception and administrative service, supporting both patients and the clinical team. This includes managing appointments, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, processing prescriptions, and maintaining accurate patient records using clinical systems such as EMIS Web. Working in a busy primary care environment, the role requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm and organised under pressure. You will play an important part in ensuring patients are directed to the right services and receive timely, appropriate care. Overall, the GP Receptionist role is vital in supporting high-quality patient care and contributing to the effective running of the NHS GP practice. Main duties of the job Provide a professional and welcoming reception service to patients, carers, and visitors Answer telephone calls promptly, deal with enquiries, and signpost patients appropriately Book, cancel, and manage appointments using clinical systems (e.g. EMIS) Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records, ensuring confidentiality at all times Scan, file, and process incoming/outgoing correspondence and clinical documents Support clinicians with administrative tasks, including referrals and follow-ups Deal with patient related admin duties such as emails, registrations and processing online consultations. Deal with patient queries in a calm and professional manner, including difficult or distressed individuals Ensure compliance with GDPR, NHS policies, and practice procedures Work effectively as part of a team in a busy, fast-paced primary care environment Job responsibilities Patient Services Act as the first point of contact for patients in person and by telephone Deal with patient enquiries in a polite, professional, and sensitive manner Book, cancel, and amend appointments accurately and efficiently Signpost patients to appropriate clinicians or services Assist with recall of patients needing annual or monitoring reviews Administration Duties Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records using clinical systems Process repeat prescription requests following practice protocols Scan, file, and manage incoming and outgoing correspondence Support administrative tasks including referrals and clinical document processing Processing patient registrations Team Support Work closely with GPs, nurses, and the wider practice team Assist with the organisation of clinics and daily workflows Support colleagues to ensure smooth and efficient service delivery Confidentiality & Compliance Maintain strict confidentiality in line with GDPR and NHS policies Follow all practice procedures, protocols, and safeguarding requirements Ensure a professional and safe reception environment at all times General Responsibilities Manage a busy workload in a fast-paced environment Remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult or distressed patients Work effectively as part of a team and support colleagues when required Participate in training and continuous development relevant to the role
